review_text: These are classic Apple, they're like magic. Assuming you have an iPhone or Apple Watch with the Ultra Wideband hardware for "Precision Finding":1. At long distance: It gives you real-time directional information to the AirTag in two-dimensional space, you get a heading plotted out on a circle, which is where the AirTag is relative to the direction you're facing, you also get the straight line distance (in whatever measurement unit you use in iOS, feet in the U.S.), just point it ahead and walk straight to it. It works at longer distances too with the second generation, in the outdoors you can probably get up to 100 feet of tracking easily.2. At close distance: It dials in with "Precision Finding", this operates in three-dimensional space instead, as you move your phone around, above you, below you, away from you, close to you, it shows you on screen in real-time if you're getting closer, this lets you home in on precisely where the item is (on the order of inches), so you don't have to search a vague area or an approximation.3. It also has the ability to emit a chime, the sound is much louder and higher in pitch in the second generation (50% louder).The setup is easy, you pull a plastic tab (which keeps the battery circuit disconnected), the circuit completes, it emits a small chime, hold it near your iPhone and it starts pairing immediately. You can assign each AirTag a unique name and emoji to identify it. These are part of the "Find My" ecosystem so it's simple to track all of your AirTags in the "Find My" app.This is one of those things you've always wanted, where after finally getting and using them you realize three things:1. Why didn't you get them earlier?2. You don't have enough of them, you need more, in fact I ended up ordering another 4-Pack.3. These make great gifts: Perfect price range for a gift, small box to wrap, extremely useful for the recipient.My first 4-Pack was used up on the following items:💰 Wallet🔑 Home, Mailbox, Miscellaneous Keyring🔑 Car Key: I don't keep other keys on the same keyring as the car key, since excessive weight can wear the tumblers in the car's ignition cylinder.🚗 Car: 3D printed a little magnetic box for it (you can just buy one as well), and hid it inside the car, in case someone steals my car.Battery replacement was made easy to keep these working indefinitely:🔋 The stainless steel cover has a leaf spring on the back side which applies outward force on the cover keeping it in place, while pushing the cover inward to overcome the leaf spring, you rotate it left/counter-clockwise to remove the cover, right/clockwise to seal the cover. The rotation will be difficult to do if your fingers or the AirTag are oily, so make sure to wash your hands and clean the AirTags with a microfiber cloth.🔋 The battery is held in place by the speaker, which is magnetic, and happens to be placed directly center under the plastic below the battery, so it holds the battery in place to prevent you from dropping the battery accidentally, great design!🔋 Instead of an expensive proprietary battery they used a standard off-the-shelf CR2032 battery, an Amazon Basics CR2032 4-Pack is around $5, they last about a year assuming you're not constantly playing sounds through them and doing "Precision Finding" often.❌ I did have one issue that wasn't an AirTag issue but a "Find My" issue. My iPhone stopped doing "Separation Alerts" entirely (the push notifications when you leave a device or AirTag behind), it's in the "Find My" app under "Notify When Left Behind At". It wasn't working for any of my devices (like my iPads) nor AirTags. The only thing that fixed it was what I read on Reddit, on your iPhone that's supposed to receive the "Separation Alerts" (the one sharing location for "Find My"), sign out of your iCloud account then sign back in, that fixed it. I noticed other issues recently like text messages not arriving until I restarted the phone, then they would all flood in at once, I think these issues were related. It's annoying because signing out of iCloud means you'll have to set some stuff up again like your Wallet payment cards, but it's not that many and it tells you what you'll have to set up again when you're signing out. If you get AirTags make sure this is working, because this feature is arguably half the reason of buying AirTags. My guess is the iCloud session becomes corrupted due to an iOS update, since that's the only major thing happening to my iPhone, so from now on I'm just going to sign out and back in after every update.If you're interested in keychain cases, after going through a few of them I settled on the one with ASIN: B0D9ND1DR2, because:1. The silicone design is simple, the AirTag sits inside firmly, the form factor of the case is very slim and lightweight so it doesn't add a big heavy thing to your keychain.2. It doesn't affect functionality, Bluetooth LE passes through silicone and plastics, the sound/chime functionality is also only muffled by about 20%, better than other cases I tested which muffled by >=50% which is unacceptable to me.3. I wanted an all-enclosing case to protect the AirTag from all sides AND hide the AirTag from a thief.4. If you choose another style case that isn't all-enclosing, where the AirTag is exposed/visible, they sell plastic film to keep the AirTag clean and free of scratches (ASIN: B096XLQ3RS), if you don't want to pay for this you can just use plastic wrap or food cling film.🖨️ If you have a 3D printer you can also design and print a variety of AirTag accessories, you can print a case that clamps onto anything you want to track. Bike? Scooter? Wheelchair? Drone? RC-Car? I designed and printed some keychain cases, luggage cases, a car case with a magnet inside that I can hide inside my car on a ferrous surface. Just download an STL model for an AirTag on Printables and use that for the hole/cavity in your design.

review_title: Easy to setup. Helps locate lost or misplaced items. Great for travel, or if you misplace things.
review_text: I bought the 4-pack for an upcoming trip. I also occasionally misplace my keys, so this will reduce frustration and time spent searching for them. They’re pricey, but that’s typical for all Apple products, and I’ve found them to be worth it. The packaging is outstanding, protects them from damage, and it’s easy to open. Setup was quick and simple. Have your iPhone nearby. Just pull the tab holding the paper covering on each airtag, and your phone will prompt you. There are categories already set up so you can label each one, i.e., keys, luggage, backpack, etc. as you activate it, and it automatically ties it to your location. There’s an option to turn off notifications for when each airtag is located at your home address. Although not required, I highly recommend purchasing AirTag holders. The AirTags are by design small and portable, and they’re also round and slick, so it’s easy to lose them if they’re not physically connected to whatever you’re trying to protect and locate if lost or misplaced. A set of 4 of the silicone ones popped up for purchase when I put the 4 pack of AirTags in my shopping cart. They help protect the AirTag, but most importantly, they allow you to securely connect the AirTag to your keys, luggage, or whatever. The ones I bought are in 4 different colors, so it’s easy for me to identify which one is which. I just got the AirTags, so I can’t say yet how reliable or accurate they are, but I’ll update this review if there are any issues.

I got the 4-pack mostly for traveling and so far I really like them. They were super easy to set up with my iPhone and I use them for my luggage, backpack, and keys.The Precision Finding works really well when the AirTag is nearby, and the speaker is loud enough that I can actually hear it inside a bag. I also really like being able to check where my luggage is when I’m traveling. It just gives me a little more peace of mind at the airport.They’re small, simple, and pretty much just work without having to mess with anything. The only thing I don’t like is that there’s still no hole for a keyring, so you have to buy a holder if you want to put one on your keys.Overall I’m really happy with them and I think the 4-pack is worth it if you have multiple things you want to keep track of.

review_title: AirTag (Gen 2) 2x Louder, 30% Thinner, 50% Longer. Too good to be true?
review_text: In depth review below summary -TLDR (too long, didn’t read summary)I didn’t think the AirTag had many ways to be improved, realistically, without a higher price point. Apple delivered all their promises though with this AirTag (2nd generation) that is more than 2x louder, 30% thinner (and lighter), while using 50% less battery.With AirTag, Apple has fixed the lost dog problem and made it so we never have to lose our keys again; the days of needing to go to the DMV to replace my lost license are in the past. Join the revolution, get your hands on AirTags! - Recommended for iPhone users, Android users look into if trackers are made by their phone’s manufacturer.In Depth Product Review:01. Sound test.Strong pass, although it honestly sounds more like 2.5-3 times as loud as my 1st gen AirTag (about 8 months old with a brand new battery). This shocked me, as the original never felt too silent by any means.02. Battery life.We’ll see - if Apple’s telling the truth. It’ll be years before we know with a new device that uses such a small amount of power. These moments used to make me tremble with anxiety, not knowing how much time it will take to replace the item.Now I simply open the “Find My” app and click the item (or puppy) and see (with impressive precision) an arrow that points in the direction of my AirTag and displays # of feet away the item is from you. You move? The arrow and distance change instantly. The item moves? Same thing. I can’t see it? I tap on ring item and even buried under a foot of dirt would hear the new, incredibly impressive speakers.Apple has fixed the lost dog problem and made it so we never have to lose our keys again; the days of needing to go to the DMV to replace a lost license are in the past for me. Join the revolution, get your AirTag’s today!Comparisons to similar products:There’s no way to disconnect or need to drown your battery life with location always being shared and Bluetooth always being connected to a device. Unlike all of the new Bluetooth often labelled “Apple Find My Supported” Bluetooth trackers in wallets and key fobs are all awful and any modern day tracker that’s using ancient (40 year old Bluetooth technology) made by anyone besides Apple.

Setup was seamless and it paired with my phone in seconds. Tracking accuracy is impressive, especially with precision finding on compatible devices. Battery life has been solid so far with no signs of draining fast. Build quality feels sturdy and small enough to fit discreetly on keys or in a bag. Genuinely useful product that's already saved me from losing track of my things more than once.

Tracking is precise, it is very thin I use it for my wallet and can name it in the find my app, stupid easy to set up and use, the size is about the size of a quarter, makes a nice gift for someone who loses things often. Highly recommended. I been using it for a few months. I don’t worry about losing g my wallet anymore.

I absolutely love my Apple AirTag\. I got it because I wanted an extra layer of security for my autistic sister, and it gives me so much peace of mind knowing I can help locate her if we ever get separated\. It’s small, easy to use, and works seamlessly with my iPhone\. I especially love that I can attach it to something she carries with her without it being bulky or uncomfortable\.For our family, it’s more than just a gadget—it gives us reassurance and an added sense of security\. I highly recommend an AirTag to anyone who wants a simple way to keep track of important belongings and have a little extra peace of mind for their loved ones\.

review_title: Compatibility and functionality on point. Highly recommend.
review_text: I have several different trackers for my many animals but the few that I have that are indoor /outdoor animals, I only trust apple tracker with these! I thought they were all the same, and they all worked pretty much the exact same however, I noticed the offbrand trackers were a little bit all the way to a lot louder than the Apple trackers but the one feature I cannot do without is when the animal is in close proximity, it gives you how many feet away as well as an arrow of what direction that animal is at and since my animals hang around my yard and never wander too much further away I needed something that was gonna be able to tell me precisely where my animals were when they were outside and that's this track tracker and only Apple! Some others do give a perfectly fine location and that's where the sound would come in, but I noticed it may say it's in one area and the sound won't play because it's too far away from that location that it's telling you to be at & I have went through several with that issue and I've always come back to this tracker.
